scalars.scalar_value: Experience serving as, or working closely with, counseling faculty and staff within the California Community Colleges.

items.item_text: 01. I understand that all requested materials have been uploaded as attachments and are required for a complete application. This includes: 1.) Resume; 2.) A cover letter addressing the listed desirable qualifications, personal and professional qualities; 3.) A list of three (3) professional references including name, position, organization, phone number, email, and relationship to the applicant; 4.) Unofficial copies of all college transcripts; 5.) Response to the following question: What does it mean to have a commitment to diversity, and how would you apply this commitment as you conduct your responsibilities in this position? Options: Yes | No
Experience serving as, or working closely with, counseling faculty and staff within the California Community Colleges.
Experience supporting instructional, counseling, and Student Services programs within a community college environment.
Knowledge of and experience with state reporting systems and accountability platforms, such as VAR, NOVA, and SARC.

Directs the implementation of departmental policy changes, policy modifications, the development of new curriculum, changes to curriculum, special assignments, action plans, and institutional effective plans to obtain short- and long-term objectives for all areas under responsibility.
Ensures that all programs under responsibility, instructional activities, policies and procedures are in compliance with state/federal/local regulations and collective bargaining agreements.
Provides administrative oversight of the Transfer Center and collaborates with the Transfer Center Director/Counselor responsible for coordinating its day-to-day operations.
Authorizes departmental personnel action.
Approves of student success in reach strategies to provide support services for students.
Approves outreach and orientation initiatives, workshops, and events.
Approves the use of financial resources for all departments and areas under responsibility.
Ensures that required assessments are completed for all departments under responsibility.
Participates in the District’s recruitment process to hire full time and part time staff; recommends the hire of full-time certificated staff to the student services executive.
Analyzes employee performance to develop performance evaluations and address performance issues for faculty, classified staff, and administrators under responsibility.
Apportions work amongst subordinate administrators, certificated staff, classified staff, and unclassified staff to ensure that the needs of all areas under responsibility are being met.
Engages in employee discipline.
Approves paid time off for all employees under supervision.
Directs the preparation of various federal, state, county, and District reports to ensure compliance with regulatory report deadlines.
Ensures that grant guidelines and outcomes are being met.
Effectively engage and support historically minoritized groups by addressing issues of equity and improving culturally responsive service-oriented practices.
Performs other duties as assigned.
Accrediting Commission for Community and Junior Colleges (ACCJC) Standards.
Maintain up to date on any changes to state/federal/local regulations to govern the area under responsibility.
Understanding of and commitment to the principles and practices of shared governance.
California Community College (CCC) Chancellor Office guidelines.
Effectively hire, appraise, discipline, and dismiss subordinate employees.
Demonstrated effectiveness in advocating for students, Student Services programs, faculty, and staff within institutional decision-making and resource allocation processes.
State regulations governing the employment of faculty and academic practices.
Sets the standard and level of service for the areas under responsibility.
Resume/Curriculum Vitae.
Federal regulations governing Title IX.
Effectively follow provisions of collective bargaining agreements, state regulations, and District policies as it pertains to the management of subordinate employees and departmental operations.
A cover letter addressing the listed desirable qualifications and personal/professional qualities.
State and Federal regulation regarding mandated reporting.
Represent the department/District in college, regional, and state meetings.
A list of three (3) professional references including name, position, organization, phone number, email, and relationship to the applicant.
District policies governing areas under responsibility.
Maintain current on any developments impacting areas under responsibility.
Unofficial copies of all college transcripts. Official sealed transcripts will be required at the time of hire.
Collective bargaining agreements.
Effectively engage and support historically minoritized groups by addressing issues of equity and improving culturally responsive service-oriented practices.
Diversity question response: What does it mean to have a commitment to diversity, and how would you apply this commitment as you conduct your responsibilities in this position?
Student learning outcome assessments (SLOs) and program review assessments.
Apportions work equitably among subordinate staff members.
Data gathering software.
Develop and maintain effective working relationships with District staff, students, and departmental visitors.
Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) Software.
General office software and equipment.
Ensure departmental programs, curriculum, are in compliance with CCC Chancellor Office standards and guidelines.
Use enterprise resource systems to view and approve budgetary requests and employee information.
Use data gathering software to run reports.
Apply knowledge of ACCJC Standards to develop accreditation reports and ensure that all programs under responsibility comply with such standards.
Communicate effectively, orally and in writing.
Knowledge of Title 5 requirements and other applicable regulations governing counseling and special programs.

Apply knowledge of state regulations District policies, and collective bargaining agreements, to ensure the supervision of employees, class schedules, faculty assignments, approve personnel actions, and budgets are in compliance.
Effective written and oral communication skills and demonstrated ability to communicate effectively with diverse constituencies within and outside the District.
Use knowledge of state and federal regulations regarding mandated reporting to organize the gathering of information and data in a timely manner to produce mandated reports.

Knowledge and understanding of institutional frameworks, including learning communities and other integrated student support models, designed to remove systemic barriers, close achievement gaps, and provide comprehensive wraparound resources for disproportionately impacted students.

Apply knowledge of SLOs and Program Reviews to ensure that such assessments are completed in an accurate, timely manner and that such assessments are used to develop/assess short/long term departmental goals and grant outcomes.

Proven ability to implement, evaluate, and continuously improve new and existing technologies that effectively and accurately support the operational and service needs of Student Services programs, faculty, and staff.
Use general office software and equipment to develop reports, aggregate data, and communicate with District staff and students.

Demonstrated ability to lead, manage, develop, and evaluate counseling and Student Services programs, including personnel, operations, budgets and resources, compliance, and continuous improvement, to effectively meet evolving student needs.
